title: Trade Systems Engineer
department: Trading Platform Tech Ops – CHIP Support
location_summary: Chicago, IL (onsite; Monday-Friday shift with weekend/holiday coverage as needed)
reason: Entry-level (1-3 years, internships/projects count) trade systems / production support role at a trading firm, matching the candidate's target of trading-firm production/infrastructure teams. Required skills (Linux, Python/Bash scripting, Docker/Kubernetes exposure, networking basics, troubleshooting) align closely with the candidate's systems administration and infrastructure experience. Onsite in Chicago, which the candidate accepts via relocation. Posting does not mention sponsorship, so it is unknown; no explicit refusal.

deep.reason: Jesse's current role owning two RHEL production servers and Linux lab infrastructure for 1,000+ users directly satisfies the posting's 1-3 years of systems administration experience and its Linux/Unix command-line requirement.

why_fit: Jesse's current role owning two RHEL production servers and Linux lab infrastructure for 1,000+ users directly satisfies the posting's 1-3 years of systems administration experience and its Linux/Unix command-line requirement.

Python, Bash, and Ansible automation experience plus Docker/Kubernetes exposure and a Prometheus/Grafana SLO-driven platform project map cleanly to DRW's scripting, containerization, and proactive issue-spotting qualifications.

Production support work on a live payments platform (JamboPay) and CI/CD ownership at Fasi Health demonstrate troubleshooting high-stakes systems with urgency and clear communication, and trading-firm production roles are Jesse's stated strongest interest.
resume_bullets: Own two RHEL production servers and Linux lab infrastructure supporting 1,000+ students, faculty, and researchers; diagnose virtualization, software, and configuration issues.
Automate provisioning and recurring tasks with Python, Bash, and Ansible.

pulse-platform: Python microservices on Kubernetes (Helm, HPA), Terraform-provisioned AWS, GitHub Actions CI/CD, and Prometheus/Grafana observability against SLOs — adapt to emphasize proactively monitoring system health, mirroring DRW's 'spotting and resolving potential issues' mandate.

gaps.gap: No direct trading or financial markets experience (exchanges, order/execution systems, market data).
gaps.address: Frame the JamboPay production payments platform and 1,000+-user sysadmin ownership as high-stakes production support, note the posting explicitly says you'll learn the trading environment on the job, and study basic market and exchange concepts before the interview.

gaps.gap: Networking exposure is home-lab level (VLANs, tcpdump/Wireshark) with no documented enterprise DNS/DHCP troubleshooting.
gaps.address: Highlight packet-level debugging and network diagnostics from the home lab and sysadmin work, and review DNS/DHCP fundamentals and common tools (dig, traceroute, ss, ping) before the first-round interview.

gaps.gap: Currently on OPT and will need H-1B sponsorship in the future.
gaps.address: Be transparent that STEM OPT provides work authorization without sponsorship for roughly the next two-plus years, so no immediate sponsorship is required, and confirm DRW's willingness to file an H-1B later early in the process.

interview_topics: A live troubleshooting scenario for a slow or unreachable trading server, expecting systematic Linux diagnostics and TCP/IP/DNS reasoning with tools like ping, ss, dig, and tcpdump.
Concrete examples of automation with Python or Bash and how you prioritize and communicate progress when resolving urgent, time-pressured production issues.
Motivation for trading-firm support work and willingness to cover weekends, holidays, and non-traditional shifts as markets move toward 24x7 trading.
